scope: Read-only engine research; no installed-game/system writes or native interactions. Evidence files are workspace copies.

provenance.metadata_type: Third-party dump of Valve-authored binary convar/command metadata and decompiled native menu; not a Valve optimization recommendation.
provenance.local_match: All video_defaults_0..3 and video_version match installed extracted resources after CRLF-to-LF normalization. Current popup_settings.vxml_c archive-entry CRC32 3895611e and size 32094 match pinned repo index. CRC32 is not cryptographic proof; normalized preset SHA256 and downloaded source SHA256 are recorded.
provenance.runtime_limit: Dumped initial/default/min/max metadata does not prove a console command is accepted or a native video setting took effect in this running process. Parent must validate after a controlled restart and benchmark.

conclusions: Prefer a short native-video profile plus release/archive FPS and telemetry controls. Do not copy hundreds of unrelated internal convars.

Console devonly/cheat restrictions, gameinfo override restrictions, and native menu video settings are distinct access paths. Menu-exposed devonly values are valid normal native-video settings; devonly in an autoexec does not imply working console access.
The current Valve Low preset is directly installed-source-backed. It has shadow quality LOW rather than an OFF option.

Remove this machine's manually inserted unsupported or hidden renderer overrides instead of forcing cheat/internal values. Restoring normal engine behavior can restore graphics work; increased FPS relative to an unsafe older profile is not guaranteed.
Preserve hardware tier knobs, display identifiers, native resolution, controls, audio and accessibility when current semantics cannot be proven.
A thousandfold FPS gain cannot be substantiated. Select the best profile using matched current-build measurements.

validation_plan.export_note: condump is release. Current binary names condump%03d.txt; help text still calls .log. Inspect created filename rather than assuming it.
validation_plan.native_readback: After game is closed and backed-up settings applied, restart normally, open native graphics menu, verify profile values and native output resolution. Re-read saved video/config files. Unsupported query errors or ignored settings must not count as changes.
validation_plan.telemetry: Native HUD frametime_show 2 is release/archive; cl_showfps is release and mode4 documents FPS logging. Reversible diagnostic use, no cheats.
validation_plan.benchmark: Warmed representative dense fight replay/camera route with same duration and scene, three or more repetitions per profile, alternate order, keep API/driver/power/background load consistent. Compare average FPS, frame-time percentiles and stutter counts; input latency needs a separate latency measurement.
validation_plan.bottleneck: Upscaling primarily lowers GPU work; CPU-limited dense scenes can stay unchanged. Use paired render-resolution variants to diagnose.
validation_plan.restrictions: No code injection, no live-process memory read/write, no DLL/VPK/gameinfo modification, no cheats or development-only unlock.

fsr_evidence.point: FSR2 has nonzero reconstruction work and temporary/persistent GPU-memory cost. AMD's published 1080p DX12 Quality examples include 0.2 ms on RX 7900 XTX and 0.5 ms on RX 6700 XT, without sharpening. These are not Deadlock/DX11/RX 7800 XT measurements.
fsr_evidence.inference: FSR1 80% is an appropriate challenger to existing FSR2 80% because it removes temporal reconstruction but retains GPU-resolution reduction. Native 1080p and FSR2 Quality must remain measured challengers; no automatic winner.
fsr_evidence.clarity: Readability, distant small targets, aliasing and motion artifacts need actual game review, not merely screenshots of config text.

concrete_core_review.verdict: No implementation blocker in BASE/native/profile settings or legacy-removal intent. Runtime verification and benchmark remain required.
findings: BASE matched current installed low preset or native menu. r_depth_of_field is active, not obsolete.
FSR1 0.8 and sharpness 0.2 fit supported sliders. FSR2 Quality 0.666667 fits current enum.
LOW shadow quality 0 is correct. Do not describe it as shadows off.
Mipmap bias 2 is native LOW. No extreme bias4/5/8.
Preserve cpu_level/mem_level/gpu_mem_level/gpu_level. Existing low-tier fields have old optimization provenance, but current semantic effect cannot be proven enough to normalize them.
Legacy-key removal does not prove performance improvement; it restores defaults for unsupported manual keys.
Duplicate removal for targeted keys and verification of one desired scalar is sensible; leave unrelated preferences intact.
No change to parent's files made.

runtime_readout_followup.task: Research-only; no connection, native UI automation, console input, listener probing, game restart or game/system write performed.
runtime_readout_followup.external_live_readout_verdict: No Valve primary documentation found that establishes a supported external read-only convar query API for this already-running retail Deadlock client. This is an evidence limitation, not a universal assertion that Source2 has no remote console or that no listener exists.
runtime_readout_followup.vconsole_scope: Accessible/indexed Valve Developer Community material describes Dota workshop interaction or Source1 netconport. It does not establish retail Deadlock client attachment under -steam -console. Some requested Source2/VConsole pages returned 403 or unavailable. Third-party TCP/protocol projects are implementations or claims, not Valve support guarantees, and were not used to attach.

current_valve_metadata.consoletool: Release/dontrecord command; opens a VConsole subtool. This does not establish an external client readout endpoint or attachment procedure.
current_valve_metadata.vconsole_rcon_server_details: Release/dontrecord/server_cannot_query convar; help explicitly concerns easy connection to a dedicated server, not this retail client.
current_valve_metadata.installed_subtools: Installed game/core/tools/vconsole_subtools.txt declares ConvarHelperTool and ConsoleHistoryHelperTool. Their m_bRequiresAppConnection=false concerns subtool launch, not proof that current retail runtime values can be obtained while disconnected or without an enabled console transport.
current_valve_metadata.readout_commands: Current pinned registry marks help, find, cvarlist, differences, print_changed_convars and condump release. Their existence is evidence for a normal manual console diagnostic path; acceptance of each requested convar still requires actual runtime output.

launch_time_logging.verdict: No current-build Valve source/documentation was found guaranteeing that -consolelog or -con_logfile causes +queries/+exec to execute after native video settings, archived settings and menu initialization finish.
launch_time_logging.distinction: Logging output and scheduling queries are separate mechanisms. Binary option strings and generic Source1 +command syntax do not establish supported current syntax, logging destination, command acceptance, settings-load order or final settled values.
launch_time_logging.claim_limit: Do not call launch-time query output a verified final profile readback unless its timing and values are checked in the actual current process. No launch options were added during this research.

runtime_readout_followup.manual_fallback: After a normal restart with the intended profile, let the main menu and settings finish loading. A human can open the already-enabled normal console, execute the prepared query-only runtime-check.cfg, then condump and inspect output/errors plus the native graphics menu. This establishes observation at the time the human chose; it does not bypass hidden/development-only access restrictions. condump writes only a diagnostic console export.
runtime_readout_followup.excluded_methods: No process memory access, arbitrary named-pipe commands, custom remote protocols, injection, hooking, insecure mode, cheats or development-only unlock. In particular an installed -concommandpipe string requiring -insecure is not an acceptable fallback.
